title: OCC Invite  #broadway #ourtown #plays #theatre #jimparsons #zoedeutch...
transcript: Our Town is a good play okay and I'm gonna ☠️ on this hill (no pun intended) there's a Broadway revival of this classic play right now and it has a pretty stacked cast including Jim Parsons, Katie Holmes Zoe Deutch, Ephraim Sykes Richard Thomas, Billy Eugene Jones, come on! this play gets a lot of hate from people who I assume just had a bad experience doing the play in high school and now have to take it out on Thornton Wilder but I'm not standing for it okay this is a very good play and it breaks my heart every goddamn time it's like Thornton Wilder splashing cold water in my face and saying “be thankful that you're alive on planet Earth, goddammit!” and then I'm sobbing (which I was) and then he's like “it's okay it's okay just go home get some rest and do better tomorrow” and I'm like “okay okay I'll try thank you” now the production of this play that's currently on Broadway is like fine like I don't really I don't care to put energy into defending it I've said before that I'm not really a fan of Kenny Leon and once again it feels like the direction is kind of all over the place here it feels like a lot of isolated attempts at boldness without really emphasizing anything that the play doesn't already emphasize perfectly well itself but I enjoyed it anyway for a few reasons first of all because Our Town is so theme-driven and concept-driven and with the lack of the 4th wall that you don't really need that much of a coherent vision for the play to work well on its own terms secondly because I think the best part of this production were the performances from Zoe Deutch and Ephram Sykes as Emily and George and they are so much of the heart and soul of the play that it really helped anchor the production and thirdly on just a personal note I think I was in a perfect position where I love this play but I haven't revisited it in like eight years and I've actually never seen it done professionally so I had the perfect amount of distance whereas I think if I had seen it a lot more recently I might have been less forgiving of the production as it stands I definitely didn't hate the production I was kind of just watching it like “okay sure” like “might as well make some choices right? but I'm pretty much only focused on the text” all of this to say that if you're already sick to ☠️ of this play this production probably isn't gonna do much to change your mind but if you haven't revisited it in a while and it even better if you've never seen or read it I think this is a really good opportunity to give it a chance
